title: Retail Inventory Reconciliation
business: Regional retail managers who need to consolidate disparate inventory and sales logs.
problem: Managers struggle with fragmented data sources where inventory counts and sales records exist in separate, non-aligned files, leading to manual reconciliation errors and stock-out risks.
solution: Pandas provides a unified framework to ingest these heterogeneous sources into DataFrames, enabling explicit data alignment through joins and powerful split-apply-combine operations via groupby to calculate net stock levels.
steps: Load inventory and sales CSV files into separate DataFrame objects.
Perform an outer join on the product ID column to align all available records.
Handle missing values resulting from the join using fillna to represent zero-stock scenarios.
Use groupby on the product category to aggregate total sales and remaining inventory.
Export the reconciled summary table for executive reporting.
outcome: A clean, unified view of inventory health that allows managers to make data-driven restocking decisions without manual spreadsheet manipulation.
limitation: Generalization often sacrifices performance; for extremely large datasets, the memory overhead of creating new objects during joins and groupby operations can become a bottleneck, which should be checked by monitoring system memory usage during execution.
